body:
FOUND BY A RAIL WRITTEN FOR SOMETHING ELSE, 2026-08-19, while giving drop-two-sided a real
byte-level assertion. MEASURED, both directions:

  two peers publishing DIFFERENT law   -> both bind; dropping one leaves the other serving. Correct.
  two peers publishing IDENTICAL law   -> the second NEVER BINDS, and the sync REPORTS IT BOUND.

    rTwo.bound contains "bob:Plant"          <- the report
    me.def("bob:Plant") throws               <- the store
    "no registered schema named bob:Plant"

THE REPORT AND THE STORE DISAGREE, which is H7 in its plainest form: an operation that says it did
something it did not do. A person reads `bound alice:Note, bob:Note` from `loam federate open` and
queries `bob_Note` to get nothing.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ITS RARITY SUGGESTS — it is not rare, it is the DEFAULT. Two peers who both
ran `loam register --stock note` have byte-identical law. That is the friend scenario exactly: Myk
and his friend both start from the stock shelf, federate to each other, and the second channel's
lens is a name that answers nothing.

THE MECHANISM, read but not yet proven to the bottom: `schemaLawAddress` deliberately EXCLUDES the
living name, so identical law from two peers has ONE law address. adoptLaw's provenance record is
minted once per (module version, alias, law address) and `adoptOne` short-circuits on an adoption it
believes already happened — so the second channel's blessing is treated as a repeat of the first and
publishes no binding under its own living name. The exclusion is correct and load-bearing (it is what
makes `as` cheap, and what makes blessing under another name the SAME law). What is missing is that
the LIVING NAME must be part of what "already adopted" means.

RAILS:
1. Two peers with byte-identical law, two channels: BOTH names bind and BOTH serve a real read.
2. The report cannot outrun the store — whatever `sync` lists in `bound` is defined and queryable.
   This is the general form and is worth asserting once for every name the report claims.
3. Two-sided: a single peer's law still binds exactly once, under exactly one name.
4. Then drop one channel and the other's lens still serves (currently unreachable — the second
   never bound, so drop-two-sided's third test was passing on a false premise and is skipped naming
   this ticket).

TIER: self-merge. It repairs a promise §46 already makes and widens nothing that gets purged.

ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND HALF THE FIX LANDED, 2026-08-19.

The mechanism is NOT what the first read guessed. adoptOne short-circuits at a named, deliberate
guard (adopt-law.ts: "Already bound, by CONTENT ADDRESS under any name: a silent witness, never a
second publish"). boundElsewhere finds the law already served, records a `witnessed` adoption, and
returns WITHOUT publishing a binding. That guard is right for its own purpose — schemaLawAddress
excludes the living name, so a module blessed twice must not bind twice.

THE BUG WAS MINE: bindArrived pushed every successful outcome into `bound`, including `witnessed`.
The report said the name serves; the store threw on it. That half is FIXED — `witnessed` is its own
field, the CLI prints what was not created and why, and the rail asserts THE GENERAL FORM: every
name a sync reports in `bound` is defined.

WHAT REMAINS is a decision rather than a repair: TWO NAMES CANNOT SERVE ONE LAW. For federation that
is the wrong answer — alice:Note and bob:Note are meant to be two readings of the same law and both
should answer. Today the second peer's data is reachable only through the first peer's name.

Options, none chosen:
- let adoptLaw publish a second binding when `as` names a living name nothing serves (the guard would
  key on (address, livingName) rather than address alone);
- bind the second name as an alias of the first, if the substrate has a shape for that;
- accept it, and make the docs say plainly that identical law federates once, under the first
  channel's name.

The first looks smallest and most correct, and it changes adoption semantics for every caller rather
than only federation. TIER: Myk's merge.
title: Two peers with identical law: the second channel reports bound and serves nothing
